blogs.title: The 'Reasonable Observer' Standard: Navigating Transformative Use in the Wake of Warhol
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Second Circuit's application of the 'transformative' use factor in Santos v. Kimmel. It explores the court's rejection of Santos's 'subjective intent' argument, focusing on how the court prioritizes the perception of a reasonable observer over the creator's internal motives. The post will discuss the implications of this for political figures who may seek to claim copyright over content that is inevitably subject to public commentary and satire.

blogs.title: Market Substitution vs. Satirical Commentary: Defining the Boundaries of Fair Use
blogs.description: Focusing on the fourth fair use factor, this post examines the court's reasoning that parody and criticism do not constitute a 'competing substitute' for the original work. It analyzes the doctrinal distinction between a use that 'usurps' a market and one that merely 'devalues' it through criticism, and how this reinforces the protections afforded to late-night media and political satire.

blogs.title: The Contractual Fortress: Standing and Third-Party Beneficiaries in Platform Terms of Service
blogs.description: This post examines the dismissal of Santos's state law contract claims, focusing on the 'strong presumption' against conferring benefits to non-contracting third parties. It explores the practical legal implications for gig-economy platforms like Cameo, arguing that the court's ruling reinforces a 'contractual fortress' that shields platforms from liability to the subjects of the content created on their sites.

blogs.title: Pleading Fraud in the Digital Age: The 'Out-of-Pocket' Hurdle
blogs.description: A technical look at the dismissal of the fraudulent inducement claim, this post discusses New York's specific requirement for 'out-of-pocket' losses. It analyzes why even a deceptive interaction on a social platform might fail to meet the pleading standards for fraud if the plaintiff cannot demonstrate a tangible monetary loss, providing a guide for practitioners on the strictness of fraud claims in high-profile media disputes.
